comments.body:
Phase 1 RCA before repair.

Step 0(a): duplicate sweep ran `rebar search "dead compact-sweep holder pid_state live"` and `rebar list --type bug --status open,in_progress`; only this bug matches the MCP stale compact-sweep holder. The open session-log `heinous-undivining-ungulate` is the incident log, not a duplicate. Closed sibling `larval-tribal-tigermoth` is same stale-pid lock class and prior-art fix pattern.

Step 0(b): created_at `1788228927503392001` -> floor `779449bd19fb96d072af58b624b9a5fa0f3b04ee`; no suspect-path changes from floor to origin/main for lock.py, lock_owner/sync/ref_lock/heartbeat. Step 0(c): worktree current at `1299d9deb6da82708bf694e19572ef8579664f34`.

Confirmed root cause: MCP `log_session` reaches the shared write lock. The waiter obtains `.ticket-write.lock` via fcntl, then polls stale `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner`. Same-host, same-namespace, `_pid_alive=True`, `_process_start_time=None` is only reclaimed after the 1h ceiling, so it burns every MCP/write timeout even though the kernel lock is free. `describe_lock_holder` also reports bare pid liveness as `pid_state=live` without start-time corroboration.

Discriminating experiment: forged same-host compact-sweep owner stamp in an isolated repo; proved kernel fcntl free by taking `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`; drove real FastMCP `log_session`; trace showed fcntl acquired, `_pid_alive(49003)=True`, `_process_start_time(49003)=None`, then timeout with `pid_state=live` and mkdir dir still present. A real MCP `log_session` in this session timed out, while local CLI append succeeded and the shared checkout had no mkdir lock dir, proving the active MCP server uses a different tracker path/clone than local CLI.

Defect origin: `larval-tribal-tigermoth` (`ab00-1407-2da3-42fd`) by plan-defect/omission. Its fix intentionally left immediate reclaim on held fcntl out; this incident proves that omission wedges MCP/write budgets. I will close with `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=larval-tribal-tigermoth` after land+Verified.

comments.body:
Step-7 sweep/parity census for avoided-flannel-eeve.

Invariant: a stale ticket-store write-lock mkdir artifact must not block a mutating operation once the waiter has obtained the authoritative same-tracker kernel fcntl leg; holder diagnostics must not label an unqualified pid-number match as a proven live owner.

Construct sweep: `rg "kill\([^,]+,\s*0\)|pid_alive|ProcessLookupError" src/rebar` found only `rebar._store.lock_owner._pid_alive` as the process-liveness probe used by lock ownership. `rg "_mkdir_lock_is_stale|stamped_file_is_stale|_stamp_is_stale|_describe_stamped_pid" src/rebar` found one staleness authority (`lock_owner._stamp_is_stale`) reached by the mkdir write lock and stamped-file locks; no duplicate staleness implementation needs a second fix.

Channel census:
- CLI command: mutating CLI paths go through `event_append` / `txn._acquire_write_lock` / `lock.write_lock`, so the shared `lock_owner` fix applies.
- MCP/API tool: `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` `log_session` -> `rebar.append_session_log` -> shared append/write lock; new `tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py` probes this surface.
- Library facade: `rebar.append_session_log`, `create/comment/edit/transition` use the same command/append seams and shared write lock.
- Automated callers: sync (`src/rebar/_store/sync.py:345`), inbound_translate, push, fsck/compact helpers all call `lock.write_lock`/`lock.acquire`, so the shared fix applies without per-caller patches.
- Dual-direction diagnostics: `describe_lock_holder` now qualifies pid_state; doctor-locks and enrich-drain are string consumers, covered by `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py` and `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`.
- Reconciler `_ref_lock.py` / `_heartbeat.py`: N/A for this dead-pid-stamp gap. They use a git-ref lease with oid/fence progress and heartbeat renewal, not pid stamps or `os.kill` liveness.
- Stamped-file locks (`enrich_drain`, compact trigger, snapshot GC): they share `stamped_file_is_stale` but have no fcntl leg, so immediate fcntl-authoritative reclaim is N/A; they retain the age ceiling and receive the diagnostic wording change.

Structural guard decision: no new structural guard. The class has a single staleness authority (`_stamp_is_stale`) and the regression/unit/interface tests exercise both the true-positive and contrast paths; a static guard would either duplicate the function-level tests or overfit implementation text rather than a portable invariant.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

On 2026-08-31 (~17:30-18:00 PDT), three consecutive MCP log_session writes failed with: `flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: host=boot-bf4c34b1-475c-4363-8ff6-aada80c3c3ab pid=49003 start=19655570 held=155-174s pid_state=live op=compact-sweep)`.

Executed incident evidence:
- `ps -p 49003` on the operator host found no process.
- `lsof /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` found no holder.
- `held=` values were non-monotonic with constant `start`, consistent with a stale stamp.
- Immediate local CLI `rebar session-log append` on the shared checkout succeeded, so this is specific to the MCP write path / MCP tracker clone.

## Confirmed root cause

MCP `log_session` uses the shared write-lock path: MCP tool -> `rebar.append_session_log` -> `session_log.append` -> `append_event` -> `lock.write_lock`. `lock.acquire` first obtains the kernel `.ticket-write.lock` fcntl leg, then polls the mkdir stamp dir `.ticket-write.lock.d`; on timeout it renders `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` through `describe_lock_holder`.

The stale mkdir owner stamp is treated as authoritative for the whole write timeout even after the waiter has acquired the kernel fcntl leg. For same-host/same-namespace v2 stamps, `_stamp_is_stale` probes the pid. If `_pid_alive(pid)` is true but `_process_start_time(pid)` is unavailable, it waits for the 1h stale ceiling. That fixed the unbounded wedge in `larval-tribal-tigermoth`, but the 1h ceiling exceeds MCP/write request budgets, so every MCP write can still burn its full timeout while the kernel lock is free.

Diagnostics have a matching gap: `_describe_stamped_pid` reports bare `_pid_alive(pid)` as `pid_state=live` without start-time corroboration, so a recycled/unqualified pid number is presented as a live holder even though it does not prove the stamped compact-sweep owner exists.

## Runtime proof

In `/Users/joeoakhart/storelock-fix`, an isolated scratch repo forged `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` as a same-host `op=compact-sweep` v2 stamp. The experiment first acquired `.ticket-write.lock` with nonblocking `fcntl`, proving the kernel lock was free, then drove real in-process FastMCP `log_session`. Instrumentation showed `_acquire_fcntl` succeeded, `_pid_alive(49003)` returned true, `_process_start_time(49003)` returned `None`, and the tool timed out with `pid_state=live`. A real MCP `rebar-log_session` call in this session timed out, while local CLI append immediately created `oxymoronic-ammonic-bats`; the shared checkout had no `.ticket-write.lock.d`, so the deployed MCP server is using a different tracker path/clone than the local CLI.

## Defect attribution

`caused_by`: `larval-tribal-tigermoth` (`ab00-1407-2da3-42fd`) by plan-defect/omission. That fix explicitly considered immediate reclaim when the fcntl leg is held and deliberately left it out; this incident proves the deferred case is necessary for MCP/write budgets. Close with `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=larval-tribal-tigermoth`.

## Fix plan

Edit `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` for the shared decision/diagnostic contract. Update all exact/string consumers of `_describe_stamped_pid` as needed: `src/rebar/_store/staging.py` (behavioral abandonment decision), `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` (drain-lock holder phrase), and `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` (operator-facing pid_state/detail). Add regression tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] MCP `log_session` with a forged same-host compact-sweep mkdir owner stamp returns without `LockTimeout` under a 1s lock budget; verified by `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py -q`.
- [ ] The MCP regression test proves the free kernel fcntl leg was acquired before stale mkdir reclaim; verified by `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py -q`.
- [ ] A same-host v2 stamp whose pid probe is unqualified is stale immediately when `fcntl_held=True`; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [ ] The same unqualified stamp remains refused while fresh when `fcntl_held=False`; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [ ] Holder diagnostics do not render an unqualified pid-number match as `pid_state=live`; verified by `tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py`.
- [ ] Holder diagnostics render a corroborated matching start time as `pid_state=live`; verified by `tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py`.
- [ ] Holder diagnostics render a differing known start time as a recycled/not-owner pid; verified by `tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py`.
- [ ] Existing lock tests still pass for corroborated-live owners; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [ ] Existing lock tests still pass for foreign-host stamps; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [ ] Existing lock tests still pass for malformed stamps; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [ ] Existing lock tests still pass for aged unprovable stamps; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [ ] Step-7 parity census is posted as a ticket comment enumerating CLI, MCP/API, library facade, automated callers, dual-direction diagnostics, reconciler ref lock, and heartbeat/stamped-file locks; verified by ticket comment before close.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py -q`
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py tests/interfaces/store/test_atomic_ticket_dir_create_021d.py -q`
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
- Ticket comment containing the Step-7 parity census before close.
